extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent applicants/attorneys
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for determining when multiple claimed inventions in a single patent application are distinct, independent, or unrelated and when a restriction requirement is proper; includes criteria for rejoinder, burden of proof, and examples. Targeted to examiners and practitioners managing claim grouping/election and restriction practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combination-Subcombination distinctness
rubrics_metrics.description: Inventions are distinct if it can be shown that (1) the combination as claimed does not require the particulars of the subcombination as claimed for patentability, and (2) the subcombination has utility by itself or in other materially different combinations (MPEP § 806.05(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 8.15 for combination-subcombination restriction. In bracket 3 specify limitations of the claimed subcombination not required by the claimed combination or evidence supporting the conclusion. In bracket 4 suggest separate utility other than used in the combination. The examiner must suggest an example of separate utility; if applicant rebuts with facts, the burden shifts to the examiner to document a viable separate utility or withdraw the requirement. See also MPEP § 806.05(c) and § 821.04 for rejoinder practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subcombination essential → not distinct (no restriction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a claimed combination requires the details of a separately claimed subcombination (the combination 'requires' the specific characteristics of the subclaim), there is usually no evidence that the combination is patentable without those details; the inventions are not distinct and a restriction must not be made or maintained (MPEP § 806.05(c) I).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the combination, as amended or originally claimed, requires all limitations of the subcombination, do not require restriction. If evidence claim ABbr is deleted or amended to require Bsp, the prior restriction should not be maintained. See MPEP § 806.05(c) and § 821.04 on rejoinder.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subcombination not essential → distinctness and restriction proper
rubrics_metrics.description: If the combination as claimed does not require the details of the subcombination and the subcombination has separate utility, the inventions are distinct and restriction is proper provided reasons exist for insisting upon restriction (e.g., serious search or examination burden) (MPEP § 806.05(c) II).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Diagram as ABbr (broad) vs Bsp (specific); omission of details in ABbr is evidence the combination does not rely on specific limitations of Bsp. Restriction requires demonstration of reasons to insist (see evidence like separate classification, different field of search, status, or non-prior-art issues). Use form paragraph 8.15 and conclude with form paragraph 8.21.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence/support for insisting upon restriction (search/examination burden)
rubrics_metrics.description: Restriction is proper only when there would be a serious search and/or examination burden if restriction were not required; such burdens can be evidenced by separate classification, status, or field of search and/or by serious examination burdens such as non-prior-art issues relevant to one invention and not the other (MPEP § 806.05(c), § 808).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When asserting restriction, the examiner must concisely state the particular reasons showing independence/distinctness and why a serious search/examination burden would result (a mere conclusion is inadequate). See MPEP § 808.02 and use appropriate form paragraphs (e.g., 8.01, 8.02, 8.14–8.20.02).

rubrics_metrics.name: Plural combinations requiring a common subcombination (linking claim practice)
rubrics_metrics.description: When an application includes a claim to a single subcombination required by plural claimed combinations that are properly restrictable, the subcombination claim is a linking claim and will be examined with the elected combination; plural combinations including the subcombination provide evidence that the subcombination has utility in more than one combination (MPEP § 806.05(d)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 8.12 to list the linking subcombination and form paragraph 8.14 for restriction between plural combinations. If an elected combination is found allowable, reconsider the propriety of the restriction and rejoin allowable subcombinations per MPEP § 821.04.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subcombinations usable together — distinctness criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Two or more claimed subcombinations, disclosed as usable together in a single combination, and which can be shown to be separately usable, are usually restrictable when the subcombinations do not overlap in scope and are not obvious variants (MPEP § 806.05(d)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To support restriction, show distinctness and reasons to insist on restriction. Each subcombination is distinct if (A) the combination does not require the particulars of the subcombination for patentability and (B) the subcombination can be shown to have utility either by itself or in another materially different combination. Use form paragraph 8.16; examiner must show one subcombination has utility other than in the disclosed combination and may suggest examples; if applicant rebuts, burden shifts to examiner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Process and apparatus for its practice — distinctness
rubrics_metrics.description: Inventions are distinct if either (1) the process as claimed can be practiced by another materially different apparatus or by hand, or (2) the apparatus as claimed can be used to practice another materially different process (MPEP § 806.05(e)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 8.17 for restriction between process and apparatus. Examiner Note suggests using examples such as (a) materially different apparatus, (b) process can be practiced by hand, (c) apparatus used to practice a materially different process. The examiner must provide reasonable examples that recite material differences; if applicant rebuts, examiner must document another materially different process/apparatus or withdraw the requirement. Conclude with form paragraph 8.21 and include form paragraph 8.21.04 when appropriate for notice of potential rejoinder.

rubrics_metrics.name: Process of making vs product made — distinctness
rubrics_metrics.description: A process of making and a product made by the process can be shown to be distinct inventions if (A) the process as claimed is not an obvious process of making the product and the process can be used to make another materially different product; or (B) the product as claimed can be made by another materially different process (MPEP § 806.05(f)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 8.18 for restriction between product and process of making. Allegations of different processes or products need not be documented, but if applicant traverses, the burden shifts to the examiner to document a viable alternative process or product or withdraw the requirement. Follow with form paragraph 8.21 and use 8.21.04 to notify applicant of potential rejoinder if product claims become allowable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apparatus and product made — distinctness
rubrics_metrics.description: An apparatus and a product made by the apparatus can be shown to be distinct inventions if either (A) the apparatus as claimed is not an obvious apparatus for making the product and the apparatus can be used to make another materially different product; or (B) the product as claimed can be made by another materially different apparatus (MPEP § 806.05(g)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 8.19 for restriction requirements between apparatus and product made. Examiner must show by example that the apparatus is not an obvious apparatus for making the product and can be used to make a different product, or that the product can be made by a materially different apparatus. Conclude with form paragraph 8.21 and consider form paragraphs 8.20 and 8.21.04 where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Product and process of using — distinctness
rubrics_metrics.description: A product and a process of using the product can be shown to be distinct inventions if either (A) the process of using as claimed can be practiced with another materially different product; or (B) the product as claimed can be used in a materially different process of using that product (MPEP § 806.05(h)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 8.20 for product and process of using restrictions. The examiner must provide an example (need not be documented). If applicant proves or provides convincing argument that the example is not workable, burden shifts to the examiner to propose another viable example or withdraw restriction. Include form paragraph 8.21.04 to notify about potential rejoinder when product/apparatus claims are allowable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Related products/processes distinctness (three-part test)
rubrics_metrics.description: Related inventions (products or processes) are distinct if: (1) the inventions as claimed are either not capable of use together or can have a materially different design, mode of operation, function, or effect; (2) the inventions do not overlap in scope (mutually exclusive); and (3) the inventions as claimed are not obvious variants (MPEP § 806.05(j), ¶ 8.14.01).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 8.14.01 to state these reasons when restricting related products or processes. If a generic or linking claim is present, see MPEP §§ 809–809.03. Conclude requirement with form paragraph 8.21. In bracket 4, explain why the inventions differ in use/design/function/effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intermediate-final product distinctness
rubrics_metrics.description: In an intermediate-final product relationship, distinctness is proven if the intermediate product is useful to make other than the final product and the species are patentably distinct (i.e., nothing of record shows they are obvious variants) (¶ 8.14 Intermediate-Final Product, MPEP § 806.05(j)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 8.14 for intermediate-final product restriction. Conclude with form paragraph 8.21. Examiner should identify why the intermediate is useful other than to make the final product (insert explanation in bracket 3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent inventions — definition and restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: Inventions as claimed are independent if there is no disclosed relationship between the inventions (they are unconnected in design, operation, and effect). If independent and there would be a serious search and/or examination burden if restriction is not required, applicant should be required to restrict to one invention (MPEP § 806.06).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: unrelated combinations with different modes, functions and effects (e.g., article of apparel vs locomotive bearing). Use form paragraphs 8.20.02 (unrelated inventions) or 8.20.03 (unrelated product and process). Examiner must insert reasons showing inventions are unrelated and follow with form paragraph 8.21.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner's obligation to state particular reasons (808.01)
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner must concisely state the particular reasons for holding inventions independent or distinct; a mere statement of conclusion is inadequate. The reasons upon which the conclusion is based should be given (MPEP § 808.01).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For a combination/subcombination, point out why the subcombination has utility by itself or in other combinations and why the combination does not require the particulars of the subcombination. Use appropriate form paragraphs (8.01, 8.02, 8.14–8.20.02) to explain distinctness/independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden of proof and shifting burden on examples/alternative uses
rubrics_metrics.description: The burden is on the examiner to provide examples or show that a subcombination or invention has utility other than in the disclosed combination; if applicant provides facts or convincing evidence that the examiner's suggested use cannot be accomplished, the burden shifts to the examiner to document another viable alternative use or withdraw the restriction requirement (various sections: MPEP § 806.05(c),(d),(e),(f),(g),(h)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples suggested by the examiner need not always be documented, but must be reasonable. When applicant elects a subcombination and claims thereto are found allowable, any dependent claims requiring all limitations of the allowable subcombination will be examined per 37 CFR 1.104; consider rejoinder practice per MPEP § 821.04.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejoinder practice when elected claims are allowable
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon determining that all claims directed to an elected combination invention are allowable, the examiner must reconsider the propriety of the restriction requirement; if a subcombination is allowable, non-elected claims requiring that subcombination must be rejoined (MPEP § 806.05(d), § 821.04).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a claim to Bsp is allowable, any claims requiring Bsp, including combination claims such as ABsp, must be considered for rejoinder. Rejoined claims will be fully examined for patentability under 37 CFR 1.104; withdrawn process claims not commensurate in scope with an allowable product/apparatus claim will not be rejoined. Use form paragraph 8.21.04 to notify applicant of potential rejoinder and double patenting implications.
